name: Event management
description: Create, edit and publish events, and manage their ticket types, add-ons and promo codes. Every write runs through the same SQL as the dashboard, as the member who created the API key: it needs that member's role now (owner or manager, as in the dashboard) as well as the route's scope, and it is recorded in the write log (GET /v1/api-writes). Writes take a JSON body, either the fields themselves or wrapped ({ "event": { … } }); form-encoded bodies work too. Any write may send an Idempotency-Key header to make a resend safe.

endpoints.description: Creates a draft event in the key's organization, optionally with its ticket types. Publishing is a separate step (POST /v1/events/:id/publish), which checks the publish blockers. Writable fields: name, description, slug, starts_at, doors_at, ends_at, timezone (IANA), currency, venue_name, venue_location, venue_address (object), category, genres, subgenres, image_url, total_tickets, purchase_limits (object), summary, description_md, faq, video_url, min_age, refund_policy, policy_notes, format (in_person / online / hybrid), what_to_bring, noindex, allow_holder_release, release_cutoff_hours, accessibility, door_name_checkin. Server-owned fields (status, org, tickets_sold, …) are refused with 400 rather than ignored. The answer includes the event's publish_blockers.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The event's fields (or send them unwrapped). name is required.

parameters.name: ticket_types
parameters.description: Up to 50 ticket types to create with it: { name, price, capacity, ticket_type, visibility, … } (see Create a ticket type).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. 8-100 letters, digits, _ . : or -. Resending a write with the same key replays the first answer (with "idempotent_replay": true) instead of doing it again; the same key on another action or target answers 400.

endpoints.description: Issues a promo code through the dashboard's voucher function: one of discount_percent (more than 0, less than 100), discount_amount (major unit) or price_override; tier_id limits it to one ticket type. code is optional (3-32 letters, digits, - or _; one is generated otherwise) and unique per event. max_uses defaults to 1, valid_hours sets an expiry, reserved_email holds it for one buyer, bypass_capacity (default true, as in the dashboard) lets it sell past a sold-out type. For free tickets use comps.
